properties.name: MEASURED 2026-09-22: adding one 40-word sentence to reconcile_verification's description made reconcile_artifacts and wall_check a NEW mutually confusable pair — neither was edited
properties.statement:
While building the loop-closure reading, one sentence was appended to reconcile_verification's served description (naming the new stamp). `every_tool_is_found_by_a_query_in_the_users_words::no_new_mutually_confusable_pair` then failed on ("reconcile_artifacts", "wall_check") — two tools whose text was untouched. Reverting only that sentence made the test pass again (5/5). The finder ranks over the whole catalogue, so a description edit shifts term weights for every tool and can move a pair that was not touched across the confusability line. Consequence for anyone editing a description: the pair a failure names need not include the tool you changed; revert-and-rerun is the quick attribution. Not root-caused further — which terms moved was not measured. The sentence was dropped rather than reworded, because the reply's `stamped` field already announces the stamp.

SECOND INSTANCE, same day, and it sharpens the lesson. Adding the doubt-trace tool as `decisions_in_doubt` made it outrank `relation_coverage` for that tool's own job ("what fraction of my decisions link to another decision"), and also made it confusable with `reconcile_verification`. Rewording the description cleared the confusable pair but NOT the ranking; adding user words to relation_coverage's description did not clear it either (and broke the 1500-char cap). Renaming the tool to `choices_in_doubt` cleared it outright. ⇒ The finder weights a tool's NAME heavily: a new tool whose name carries a common noun ("decisions") can take another tool's job by name alone. Name a new tool in the asker's word ("choices"), not the design's type name. Side effect of the rewording: two long-standing baseline pairs came apart and were removed.

THIRD INSTANCE, 2026-09-27 (counted; appended), and this time the mechanism was measured. Building the address watch, the external_dependency and upstream_status descriptions grew. The full workspace run then failed no_new_mutually_confusable_pair on three pairs, none involving either tool: (answer_question, answers), (claim_report, design_identity), (release_claim, release_report). Putting back main's two descriptions with all the code kept made it pass, which is the attribution. WHY, MEASURED with the binary's own find_tools: for design_identity's query ("what design am I connected to right now"), upstream_status had held 5th place as incidental filler (it says "design" many times). Made longer, it fell to 6th at 8.54, just under claim_report at 8.64, so claim_report entered design_identity's top 5 and the pair formed. BM25's length normalisation means a LONGER description scores LOWER on every term it already had, so tools elsewhere shuffle into the slots it vacates. Four rewordings each moved the failure to a different pair. So did sharpening design_identity (dropping "right now" made (add_contributor, claim_report) a pair and broke a rank). WHAT CLEARED IT: a LENGTH-NEUTRAL edit (upstream_status at 1,311 characters against main's 1,312), plus leaving external_dependency's description as it was, since a new parameter documents itself in the schema. LESSON: when a tool gains a parameter, first try putting the words in the parameter's doc and swapping words in the description, not adding to it.
